key_provisions_or_claims: Defines automated driving systems as SAE J3016 level 4-5 systems operating without human intervention.
Permits ADS to drive if capable of complying with all applicable state and federal laws (safe harbor).
Preempts state agencies and local governments from setting ADS standards different from those for human drivers.
Testing of non-compliant ADS requires Colorado State Patrol and CDOT approval; violation is a Class B traffic infraction with possible impoundment.
CDOT must report annually on ADS testing; crash liability follows existing state, federal and common law.
annotation.summary_en: Colorado Senate Bill 17-213 authorizes automated driving systems (SAE levels 4-5) to operate motor vehicles statewide, creating a safe harbor if systems comply with applicable laws, preempting local rules, requiring state approval for testing non-compliant systems, mandating annual CDOT reports, and leaving crash liability to existing law.
annotation.title_clean: Senate Bill 17-213: Concerning Authorization for Automated Driving Systems to Control Motor Vehicles Throughout Colorado
